law.title: Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations (Northern Ireland)

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223" NumberOfProvisions="15" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/body" NumberOfProvisions="15" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Consequential amendments to the Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1993</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4" id="regulation-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/1" id="regulation-4-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1993<FootnoteRef Ref="f00007"/> shall be amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/2" id="regulation-4-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>For regulation 3(1)(a), substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>a workplace which is or is in or on a ship, save that regulations 8(1) and (3) and 12(1) and (3) apply to such a workplace where the work involves any of the relevant operations in—</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>a shipyard, whether or not the shipyard forms part of a harbour or wet dock; or</Text></P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para><Text>dock premises, not being work done —</Text><P5>
<Pnumber>aa</Pnumber>
<P5para><Text>by the master or crew of a ship;</Text></P5para>
</P5>
<P5>
<Pnumber>bb</Pnumber>
<P5para><Text>on board a ship during a trial run;</Text></P5para>
</P5>
<P5>
<Pnumber>cc</Pnumber>
<P5para><Text>for the purpose of raising or removing a ship which is sunk or stranded; or</Text></P5para>
</P5>
<P5>
<Pnumber>dd</Pnumber>
<P5para><Text>on a ship which is not under command, for the purpose of bringing it under command;</Text></P5para>
</P5>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/3" id="regulation-4-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In regulation 3(1)(c), substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>a workplace located below ground at a mine.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/4" id="regulation-4-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Omit regulation 3(1)(d).</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/5" id="regulation-4-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After regulation 3(4), add—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>As respects any workplace which is located at a quarry or above ground at a mine, regulation 12 shall only apply to a floor or traffic route which is located inside a building.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/6/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/4/6" id="regulation-4-6">
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After regulation 3(5), add—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>For the purposes of this regulation—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>“dock premises” means any dock, wharf, quay, jetty or other place at which ships load or unload goods or embark or disembark passengers, together with neighbouring land or water which is used or occupied, or intended to be used or occupied, for those or incidental activities, and any part of a ship when used for those or incidental activities;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>“relevant operations” means, in relation to a ship, its repairing, refitting, painting and finishing, the scaling, scurfing or cleaning of its boilers (including combustion chambers or smoke boxes) and the cleaning of its bilges or oil-fuel tanks or any of its tanks last used for carrying oil;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>“ship” includes all vessels and hovercraft which operate on water or land and water;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>“shipyard” means any yard or dry dock (including the precincts thereof) in which ships or vessels are constructed, reconstructed, repaired, refitted or finished; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>e</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>“vessel” means any description of craft used for the transport of goods or passengers or the storage of goods or the accommodation of passengers on water, whether used in navigation or not.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

law.title: Work at Height Regulations (Northern Ireland)

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223" NumberOfProvisions="15" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/body" NumberOfProvisions="15" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Consequential Amendments to the Work at Height Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2005</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5" id="regulation-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5/1" id="regulation-5-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Work at Height Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2005<FootnoteRef Ref="f00008"/> shall be amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5/2" id="regulation-5-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After regulation 8, insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="secondary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" NumberFormat="default">
<P1group>
<Title>Dock Operations</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">8A</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In relation to work at height where people are engaged in dock operations, every employer shall ensure that Schedule 10 is complied with.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/223/regulation/5/3" id="regulation-5-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After Schedule 9, add—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="schedule" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" TargetClass="unknown" NumberFormat="default">
<Schedule NumberFormat="default">
<Number>SCHEDULE<Character Name="NonBreakingSpace"/>10</Number>
<TitleBlock>
<Title>REQUIREMENTS FOR WORK IN DOCKS</Title>
</TitleBlock>
<Reference>Regulation 8A</Reference>
<ScheduleBody>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">1</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In relation to work at height where people are engaged in dock operations, there shall be secure and adequate guardrails at the following places—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>every break, dangerous corner and other dangerous part or edge of a dock, wharf, quay or jetty; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>every open side of a gangway, footway over a bridge, caisson or dock gate,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<Text>except in so far as the provision of such guardrails is impracticable because of the nature of the work carried out there and the work is in progress.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In this Schedule—</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“dock gate” means any lock gate or other gate which can close off the entrance to the dock or part of the dock from the sea or other waterway but does not include any gate on land which controls access by vehicles or pedestrians;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“dock operations” means—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the loading or unloading of goods on or from a ship at dock premises;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the embarking or disembarking of passengers on or from a ship at dock premises;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>any activity incidental to the activities in sub-paragraph (a) or (b) which takes place on dock premises, including any of the following—</Text><OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="roman">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the fuelling and provisioning of a ship;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the mooring of a ship;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the storing, sorting, inspecting, checking, weighing or handling of goods;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the movement of goods, passengers or vehicles;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the use of welfare amenities in relation to the activities in sub-paragraph (a), (b) or (c)(i) to (iv);</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>attending dock premises for the purposes of the activities in sub-paragraph (a), (b) or (c)(i) to (v); or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the embarking or disembarking on or from a ship of its crew at dock premises,</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
<Text>but does not include—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>the loading or unloading of goods or embarking or disembarking of persons on or from a pleasure craft or any activity incidental to those activities; or</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>e</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>beach landing operations wholly carried out by serving members of Her Majesty’s Forces or visiting forces within the meaning of the provisions of Part 1 of the Visiting Forces Act 1952<FootnoteRef Ref="f00009"/> or a combination of both;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“dock premises” means any dock, wharf, quay, jetty or other place at which ships load or unload goods or embark or disembark passengers, together with neighbouring land or water which is used or occupied, or intended to be used or occupied, for those or incidental activities, and any part of a ship when used for those or incidental activities;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“freight container” means a container as defined in regulation 2 of the Freight Containers (Safety Convention) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1992<FootnoteRef Ref="f00010"/>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“goods” includes—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>animals;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>pallets and freight containers;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>waste;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>solid ballast;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>vehicles which are being transported as cargo;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“pleasure craft” means any description of vessel when used solely for sport or recreation, other than for carrying fare paying passengers;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“ship” includes all vessels and hovercraft which operate on water or land and water;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“vehicle” includes all lift trucks, locomotives and rolling stock, and trailers and semi-trailers and other mechanical plant which moves on wheels, tracks, skids or any combination thereof;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“vessel” means any description of craft used for the transport of goods or passengers or the storage of goods or the accommodation of passengers on water, whether used in navigation or not;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“welfare amenities” means—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>sanitary conveniences;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>baths and shower baths;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>washing facilities;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a supply of wholesome drinking water;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a supply of protective clothing, that is to say, clothing suitable for the protection of the wearer in refrigerated spaces or against dirt from handling dirty goods or against inclement weather;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>accommodation and facilities for changing into clothing worn during working hours and for storing and drying clothing;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>canteens, or accommodation and facilities (including facilities for heating food and boiling water) for workers employed at dock premises to eat meals provided by themselves;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>shelters for use during inclement weather.</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P1para>
</P1>
</ScheduleBody>
</Schedule>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

law.title: Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations (Northern Ireland)

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265" NumberOfProvisions="25" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/body" NumberOfProvisions="19"><P1group><Title>Amendment of the Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4" id="regulation-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/1" id="regulation-4-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996<FootnoteRef Ref="f00013"/> are amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/2" id="regulation-4-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In regulation 2(1), after the definition of “acoustic signal” insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double">
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“the <Abbreviation Expansion="Regulation EC 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures, amending and repealing Directives 67/548/EEC and 1999/45/EC, and amending Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006">CLP Regulation</Abbreviation>” means Regulation <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/regulation/2008/1272" id="c00005" Class="EuropeanCommission" Year="2008" Number="1272">(EC) No 1272/2008</Citation> of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures, amending and repealing Directives <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1967/0548" id="c00006" Class="EuropeanEconomicCommunityDirective" Year="1967" Number="548">67/548/<Acronym Expansion="European Economic Community">EEC</Acronym></Citation> and <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/directive/1999/0045" id="c00007" Class="EuropeanUnionDirective" Year="1999" Number="45">1999/45/<Acronym Expansion="European Community">EC</Acronym></Citation> and amending Regulation <Citation URI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/european/regulation/2006/1907" id="c00008" Class="EuropeanCommission" Year="2006" Number="1907">(EC) No. 1907/2006</Citation>, of which Articles 6(5), 11(3), 12, 14, 18(3)(b), 23, 25 to 29, 35(2) second and third sub-paragraphs and Annexes I to <Acronym Expansion="7">VII</Acronym> are to be read as amended from time to time;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/3" id="regulation-4-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In regulation 3(a)—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/3/a/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/3/a" id="regulation-4-3-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>for “dangerous” substitute “hazardous”; and</Text>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/3/b/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/3/b" id="regulation-4-3-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>for “preparation” substitute “mixture”.</Text>
</P3para></P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4" id="regulation-4-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In Schedule 1—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/a/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/a" id="regulation-4-4-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in Part I, for paragraph 12 substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">12</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>Areas, rooms or enclosures used for the storage of significant quantities of hazardous substances or mixtures shall be indicated by a suitable warning sign taken from paragraph 3.2 of Part II, or marked as provided in paragraph 1 of Part III, unless the labelling of individual packages or containers is adequate for this purpose. If there is no equivalent warning sign in paragraph 3.2 of Part II to warn about hazardous chemical substances or mixtures, the relevant hazard pictogram, as laid down in Annex V to the CLP Regulation, shall be used.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>; and</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/b/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/b" id="regulation-4-4-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in Part II, after paragraph 2.2 insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">2.3</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>The “General danger” warning sign shall not be used to warn about hazardous substances or mixtures, except for cases where the warning sign is used to indicate stores of a number of hazardous substances or mixtures in accordance with paragraph 5 of Part III of Schedule 1 to these Regulations.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>;</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/c/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/c" id="regulation-4-4-c">
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph 3.2 of Part II, delete the warning sign for ‘Harmful or irritant material’;</Text>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/d/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/d" id="regulation-4-4-d">
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in Part III—</Text>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/d/i/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/d/i" id="regulation-4-4-d-i">
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>for paragraph 1 substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" Format="double"><P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">1</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>Containers used at work for chemical substances or mixtures classified as hazardous according to the criteria for any physical or health hazard class in accordance with the CLP Regulation, and containers used for storage of such hazardous substances or mixtures, together with the visible pipes containing or transporting such hazardous substances or mixtures, shall be labelled with the relevant hazard pictograms in accordance with that Regulation.</Text>
</P1para>
<P1para>
<Text>Paragraph 1 does not apply to containers used at work for brief periods nor to containers whose contents change frequently, provided that alternative adequate measures are taken, in particular for information and/or training which guarantee the same level of protection.</Text>
</P1para>
<P1para>
<Text>The labels referred to in paragraph 1 may be:</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="dash">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>replaced by warning signs as provided for in Part II, using the same pictograms or symbols. If there is no equivalent warning sign in Schedule 1, Part II, the relevant hazard pictogram, as laid down in Annex V to the CLP Regulation shall be used.</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>supplemented by additional information, such as the name and/or formula of the hazardous substance or mixture and details of the hazard.</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>for the transporting of containers at the place of work, supplemented or replaced by signs applicable throughout the Union for the transport of hazardous substances or mixtures.</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P1para>
</P1>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>; and</AppendText>
</P4para></P4>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/d/ii/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2015/265/regulation/4/4/d/ii" id="regulation-4-4-d-ii">
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>in paragraph 5, for “dangerous substances or preparations”, in both places where it occurs substitute “hazardous substances or mixtures”.</Text>
</P4para></P4>
</P3para></P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

<Title>Consequential amendments</Title>
</TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><P1group><Title>Amendment of the Ionising Radiations Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2017</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1" id="schedule-4-paragraph-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/1" id="schedule-4-paragraph-1-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Ionising Radiations Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2017<FootnoteRef Ref="f00014"/> are amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/2" id="schedule-4-paragraph-1-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In regulation 2(1) (interpretation)—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/2/a/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/2/a" id="schedule-4-paragraph-1-2-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>for the definition of “carers and comforters” substitute—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double">
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“carers and comforters” means individuals knowingly and willingly incurring an exposure to ionising radiation by helping, other than as part of their occupation, in the support and comfort of individuals undergoing or having undergone a medical exposure (other than as a carer and comforter);</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>;</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/2/b/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/nisr/2018/17/schedule/4/paragraph/1/2/b" id="schedule-4-paragraph-1-2-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in the definition of “medical exposure”, after paragraph (d), insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double">
<P3>
<Pnumber>e</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>carers and comforters;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P3para></P3>

http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1972/28/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1972/28/body" NumberOfProvisions="11"><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1972/28/crossheading/amendments-of-factories-act-1961" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1972/28/crossheading/amendments-of-factories-act-1961" NumberOfProvisions="9" id="crossheading-amendments-of-factories-act-1961"><Title> Amendments of Factories Act 1961</Title><P1group><Title> Medical examinations of persons employed in factories. <CommentaryRef Ref="c822781"/></Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1972/28/section/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1972/28/section/3" id="section-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><Text>The Factories Act 1961 shall have effect as if the following section were inserted after section 10 thereof:—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P1group Layout="below"><Title/><P1><Pnumber PuncAfter="">10A</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>If an employment medical adviser is of opinion that ther ought, on grounds mentioned in subsection (2) below, to be a medical examination of a person or persons employed in a factory, he may serve on the occupier of the factory a written notice stating that he is of that opinion and requiring that the occupier shall permit a medical examination in accordance with this section of the person or persons in question, and the examination shall be permitted accordingly.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The grounds on which a medical examination of a person may be required by an employment medical adviser’s notice under subsection (1) above are that (in the adviser’s opinion) the persons health has been or is being injured, or it is possible that it has been, is being or will be injured, by reason of the nature of the work he is or has been called upon to do or may (to the adviser’s knowledge) be called upon to do ; and a notice under that subsection may be given with respect to one or more named persons or to persons of a class or description specified in the notice.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A notice under subsection (1) above shall name the place where the medical examination is to be conducted and, if it is a place other than the factory, the day on which and the time at which it is to be begun ; and—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>every person to whom the notice relates shall be informed, as soon as practicable after service thereof, of the contents thereof and of the fact that he is free to attend for the purpose of submitting to the examination ; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>if the notice states that the examination is to be conducted at the factory, suitable accomodation therat shall be provided for the conduct of the examination.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A medical examination conducted in pursuance of a notice under subsection (1) above shall be begun within seven days after the day on which the notice is served, and shall be conducted by, or in accordance with arrangements made by, an employment medical adviser, and take place at a reasonable time during working hours.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>An employment medical adviser may, by written notice served on the occupier of a factory, cancel a notice served on the occupier under subsection (1) above ; and a notice which relates to two or more named persons may be cancelled either in relation to them all or in relation to any one or more of them.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this section “ medical examination” includes pathological, physiological and radiological tests and similar investigations.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></BlockAmendment></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

id="section-17-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an Act repeals a previous enactment and substitutes provisions for the enactment repealed, the repealed enactment remains in force until the substituted provisions come into force.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1978/30/section/17/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1978/30/section/17/2" id="section-17-2" RestrictStartDate="2020-12-01"><Pnumber><CommentaryRef Ref="c11097341"/><CommentaryRef Ref="c21791641"/><CommentaryRef Ref="c21791651"/><CommentaryRef Ref="key-2605ba"/><CommentaryRef Ref="key-2a8aa7"/><CommentaryRef Ref="key-dbe991"/><CommentaryRef Ref="key-8ce77d"/><CommentaryRef Ref="M_C_24080f7d-6eec-4be4-f109-9047681e47ab"/><CommentaryRef Ref="key-089d5a"/><CommentaryRef Ref="key-39a533"/>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an Act repeals and re-enacts, with or without modification, a previous enactment then, unless the contrary intention appears,—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1978/30/section/17/2/a" enactment so repealed shall be construed as a reference to the provision re-enacted;</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1978/30/section/17/2/b" under that provision.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

xmls: <Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40" NumberOfProvisions="140" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2020-12-31"><Primary><Schedules RestrictStartDate="2020-12-31"><Title> SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1" NumberOfProvisions="12" id="schedule-1" RestrictExtent="S" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01"><Number>SCHEDULE 1</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Setting and alteration of certain penalties</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/crossheading/increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/crossheading/increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences" NumberOfProvisions="1" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01" id="schedule-1-crossheading-increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences"><Title> Increase of fines for certain summary offences</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01" BlanketAmendment="true" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/1" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The enactments specified in column 2 of Part II of Schedule 2 to this Act, which relate to the maximum fines for the offences mentioned (and broadly described) in column 1 of that Schedule, shall have effect as if the maximum fine that may be imposed on summary conviction of any offence so mentioned were a fine not exceeding the amount specified in column 4 of that Schedule instead of a fine not exceeding the amount specified in column 3 of that Schedule (being the amount of the maximum fine in respect of the offence immediately before the passing of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8315571"/>Criminal Law Act 1977), but this sub-paragraph shall not alter the maximum daily fine, if any, provided for by any of those enactments.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/2" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In section 203 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8315581"/>Local Government (Scotland) Act 1973 (offences against byelaws), except as applied to byelaws made under any provision contained in a local or private Act other than by a local authority, for any reference to £20 there shall be substituted a reference to £50.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subject to sub-paragraph (4) below, this sub-paragraph applies to any pre-1949 enactment however framed or worded which—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>as regards any summary offence makes a person liable on conviction thereof to a fine of, or not exceeding, a specified amount less than £50 which has not been altered since the end of 1948 (and is not altered by this Act); or</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>confers power by subordinate instrument to make a person, as regards any summary offence (whether or not created by the instrument), liable on conviction thereof to a fine of, or a maximum fine of, less than £50 which has not been altered since the end of 1948 (and is not altered by this Act).</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/4" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Sub-paragraph (3) above does not apply to any offence to which section 292(2)(b) of the Principal Act applies (offences triable only summarily other than by virtue of express provision).</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Every enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies shall have effect as if for the specified amount less than £50 there mentioned there were substituted—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>£25 if the specified amount is less than £20; or</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>£50 if the specified amount is not less than £20.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/6" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/6" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-6"><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where, by virtue of any enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies by virtue of sub-sub-paragraph (a) of that sub-paragraph, a person convicted of a summary offence would, apart from this paragraph, be liable to a fine, or maximum fine, of one amount in the case of a first conviction and of a different amount in the case of a second or subsequent conviction, sub-paragraph (5) above shall apply separately in relation to each specified amount less than £50, even if this produces the same instead of different amounts for different convictions.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/7" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-7"><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Sub-paragraph (3) above does not apply to so much of any enactment as, in whatever words, makes a person liable or provides for a person to be made liable, on summary conviction, to a fine or a maximum fine for each period of a specified length during which a continuing offence is committed.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/8" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/8" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-8"><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies provides or confers a power to provide for, on conviction of an offence triable only summarily, a fine or a maximum fine in respect of a specified quantity or a specified number of things, “<Term id="term-the-specified-amount">the specified amount</Term>” for the purposes of subsection (5) above is the fine or maximum fine so provided or for which provision may be made.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/9" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/9" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-9"><Pnumber>9</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In sub-paragraph (3) above “<Term id="term-pre-1949-enactment">pre-1949 enactment</Term>” means an enactment passed before 1st January 1949 or an enactment passed on or after that date which whether directly or, through successive re-enactments, indirectly re-enacts with or without modification an enactment passed before that date.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/10" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/10" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-10"><Pnumber>10</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this paragraph, “<Term id="term-enactment">enactment</Term>” does not include an enactment contained in an order, regulation or other instrument made under an Act.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/1/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/1/b" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-1-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>were specified in the third column of Schedule 1 to that Act.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/2" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (1) of section 15 of the 1974 Act (health and safety regulations), regulations under that section may repeal or modify any of the provisions mentioned in sub-paragraph (1) above.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/3" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Nothing in sub-paragraph (1) above shall affect the operation of section 18 of the 1974 Act (enforcement of relevant statutory provisions) in relation to any time before such day as the Secretary of State may by order made by statutory instrument appoint, and different days may be appointed for different purposes.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657" NumberOfProvisions="36" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/body" NumberOfProvisions="19" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Repeals, revocations and savings</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19" id="regulation-19">
<Pnumber>19</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/1" id="regulation-19-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The provisions of—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/1/a/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/1/a" id="regulation-19-1-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the Mines and Quarries Act 1954<FootnoteRef Ref="f00010"/> specified in column 1 of Part I of Schedule 8; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/1/b/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/1/b" id="regulation-19-1-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the Factories Act 1961<FootnoteRef Ref="f00011"/> specified in column 1 of Part II of Schedule 8,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<Text>are repealed to the extent set out in the entry opposite thereto in the corresponding entry in column 2 of the respective Part.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/2" id="regulation-19-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The Hydrogen Cyanide (Fumigation) Act 1937<FootnoteRef Ref="f00012"/> is repealed.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/3" id="regulation-19-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The regulations and orders specified in column 1 of Schedule 9 are revoked or, where expressly stated, modified to the extent set out in the entry opposite thereto in column 2 of that Schedule.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1988/1657/regulation/19/4" id="regulation-19-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Any record or register required to be kept under any regulations or orders revoked by paragraph (3) shall, notwithstanding those revocations, be kept in the same manner and for the same period as if these Regulations had not been made, except that the Health and Safety Executive may approve the keeping of records at a place or in a form other than at the place where, or in the form in which, records were required to be kept under the regulations or orders so revoked.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

law.title: Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations

the 1992 regulations.title: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1992

xmls:
SCHEDULE 3 MODIFICATIONS OF THE WORKPLACE (HEALTH, SAFETY AND WELFARE) REGULATIONS 1992 Regulation 11
Column 1Column 2
ProvisionExtent of modification
Regulation 2 In paragraph (1) insert the following words as a sub-paragraph before the definition of “new workplace”— “mine” means a mine within the meaning of the Mines and Quarries Act 1954; In paragraph (1) insert the following words as a sub-paragraph before the definition of “traffic route”— “quarry” means a quarry within the meaning of the Mines and Quarries Act 1954;
Regulation 3 Replace sub-paragraph (c) of paragraph (1) with the words ; or c a workplace located below ground at a mine. .
Regulation 3Revoke sub-paragraph (d) of paragraph (1).
Regulation 3 Insert the following paragraph after paragraph (4)— 5 As respects any workplace which is at a quarry or above ground at a mine regulation 12 shall only apply to a floor or traffic route which is located inside a building. .

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1995/3162/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1995/3162" NumberOfProvisions="3" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1995/3162/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1995/3162/body" NumberOfProvisions="3" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Fees Payable</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1995/3162/article/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/1995/3162/article/2" id="article-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In each enactment specified in column (2) in relation to which there is an entry in column (5), for the sum specified in column (5) there is substituted the sum specified in relation to it in column (4); and the fee payable in England and Wales under each of the enactments specified in column (2) in respect of a matter or case specified in column (3) is that specified in relation to that matter or case in column (4).</Text>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

law.title: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978" NumberOfProvisions="4" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/body" NumberOfProvisions="2" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Amendment of the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2" id="regulation-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002<FootnoteRef Ref="f00004"/>—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/a/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/a" id="regulation-2-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (1) of regulation 2, after the definition of “mine” add the following definition–</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" Format="default" NumberFormat="default">
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>“mutagen” means a substance or preparation which if classified in accordance with the classification provided for by regulation 4 of the Chemicals (Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply) Regulations 2002<FootnoteRef Ref="f00005"/> would be in the category of danger, mutagenic (category 1) or mutagenic (category 2) whether or not the substance or preparation would be required to be classified under those Regulations;;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</BlockAmendment>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/b/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/b" id="regulation-2-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (5) of regulation 7–</Text>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/b/i/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/b/i" id="regulation-2-b-i">
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>after the word “carcinogen” add the words “or mutagen”, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/b/ii/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/b/ii" id="regulation-2-b-ii">
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>in each place where it occurs, after the word “carcinogens” add the words “or mutagens”;</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/c/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/c" id="regulation-2-c">
<Pnumber>c</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in paragraph (4) of regulation 13, for the words “carcinogen or biological agent” substitute “carcinogen, mutagen or biological agent”; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/d/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2003/978/regulation/2/d" id="regulation-2-d">
<Pnumber>d</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>at the end of Schedule 1 add the following substances–</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" Format="default" NumberFormat="default">
<P3para>
<Text>The following polychlorodibenzodioxins:</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none">
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>2,3,7,8-TCDD</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,7,8-PeCDD</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,4,7,8-HxCDD</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,6,7,8-HxCDD</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,7,8,9-HxCDD</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,4,6,7,8-HpCDD</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>OCDD,</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P3para>
<P3para>
<Text>The following polychlorodibenzofurans:</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none">
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>2,3,7,8-TCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>2,3,4,7,8-PeCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,7,8-PeCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,4,7,8-HxCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,7,8,9-HxCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,6,7,8-HxCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>2,3,4,6,7,8-HxCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,4,6,7,8-HpCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>1,2,3,4,7,8,9-HpCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para>
<Text>OCDF</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P3para>
<P3para>
<Text>Where T=tetra, Pe=penta, Hx=hexa, Hp=hepta and O=octa.</Text>
</P3para>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText></P3para>
</P3>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3363/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2004/3363" NumberOfProvisions="13" xml:lang="en" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3363/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2004/3363/body" NumberOfProvisions="13" NumberFormat="default"><P1group><Title>Health and Safety At Work Act 1974</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2004/3363/article/5" id="article-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/1" id="article-5-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Section 28 of the Health and Safety At Work Act 1974<FootnoteRef Ref="f00006"/> (restrictions on disclosure of information) is amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/2" id="article-5-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In subsection (3), after paragraph (e), insert–</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default" NumberFormat="default">
<P3>
<Pnumber>f</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>any other disclosure of information by the recipient, if–</Text>
<P4>
<Pnumber>i</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>the recipient is, or is acting on behalf of a person who is, a public authority for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, and</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
<P4>
<Pnumber>ii</Pnumber>
<P4para>
<Text>the information is not held by the authority on behalf of another person.</Text>
</P4para>
</P4>
</P3para>
</P3>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/3" id="article-5-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In subsection (5), after “disclosed in pursuance of”, insert “any of paragraphs (a) to (e) of”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/4/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2004/3363/article/5/4" id="article-5-4">
<Pnumber>4</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After subsection (9) insert–</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" Format="default" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>9A</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Subsection (7) above does not apply if–</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the person who has obtained any such information as is referred to in that subsection is, or is acting on behalf of a person who is, a public authority for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>the information is not held by the authority on behalf of another person.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>

<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>Schedule 1 to the Corporate Manslaughter and Corporate Homicide Act 2007 (list of government departments <Abbreviation Expansion="Et cetera" xml:lang="la">etc</Abbreviation>) is amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2008/396/article/2/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2008/396/article/2/2" id="article-2-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>At the appropriate places, insert “Department for Business, Enterprise and Regulatory Reform”, “Department for Children, Schools and Families”, “Department for Innovation, Universities and Skills” and “Ministry of Justice (including the Scotland Office and the Wales Office)”.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2008/396/article/2/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2008/396/article/2/3" id="article-2-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>Omit “Department for Constitutional Affairs (including the Scotland Office and the Wales Office)”, “Department for Education and Skills”, “Department of Trade and Industry”, “Office of the Deputy Prime Minister” and “Privy Council Office”.</Text>
</P2para>

xmls:
Amendment of Regulations2The Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 are amended in accordance with regulations 3 to 15.Interpretation – General31In regulation 2, the Table in paragraph (5) is amended as follows.2For the row containing the expression and meaning of “conformity mark”, substitute—
“conformity mark”The mark referred to in article 14 of the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive, the form of the mark being set out in article 15 of that Directive.
3Before the row in which the expression “conformity mark” is given a meaning, insert—
“conformity assessment”The assessment and the procedure for assessment of conformity set out in the Directives.
4After the row in which the expression “the Dangerous Goods Directive” is given a meaning, insert—
“the Directives”The Dangerous Goods Directive and the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive.
5After the row in which the expression “relevant authority” is given a meaning, insert—
“relevant member State”A member State of the EU on whose market the equipment in question has been made available.
6After the row in which the expression “the security provisions” is given a meaning, insert—
“TPED competent authority”The GB competent authority or the competent national authority in respect of the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive in Northern Ireland or another member State of the EU.
7For the row containing the expression and meaning of “the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive”, substitute—
“the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive”Directive 2010/35/EU of the European Parliament and the Council of 16 June 2010 on transportable pressure equipment and repealing Council Directives 76/767/EEC, 84/525/EEC, 84/526/EEC, 84/527/EEC and 1999/36/EC .

The Secretary of State for Energy and Climate ChangeThe carriage is national carriage and the authorisation relates to prohibitions and requirements arising out of functions for which the Secretary of State for Energy and Climate Change is the GB competent authority.
Obligations relating to the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive71For regulation 19, substitute—Scope of Obligations191Regulations 19A to 19F apply to transportable pressure equipment within the scope of the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive by virtue of article 1(2)(a) of that Directive.2For the avoidance of doubt, any reference in those regulations to a manufacturer, importer, distributor, owner or operator as “it” is not to be construed as excluding a natural person..2After regulation 19, insert—General Obligations19A1A manufacturer, importer, distributor, owner or operator may only place or make available on the market, put into service or use equipment if it ensures that the equipment meets the requirements of the Dangerous Goods Directive.2 On receipt of a request from the Health and Safety Executive, a manufacturer, importer, distributor, owner or operator must identify to the Executive any manufacturer, importer, distributor or owner who has supplied it with, or to whom it has supplied, equipment over at least the previous 10 years.3A request made pursuant to paragraph (2) must—abe in writing; andbcontain a date by which a response is to be provided with that date being reasonable in all the circumstances.4Paragraph (5) applies where a manufacturer, importer, distributor or owner provides to an operator information about equipment it has placed or made available on the market, or put into service.5The information must comply with the Directives.6This regulation does not apply to an owner who is a private individual using or intending to use equipment in the circumstances set out in article 8(4) of the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive.Obligations of Manufacturers19B1A manufacturer must—aensure a conformity assessment is carried out by a notified body;bmark equipment in accordance with articles 14 and 15 of the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive; andckeep the technical documentation specified in the Dangerous Goods Directive for the period specified in that Directive.2Where a manufacturer knows or has reason to believe that equipment it has placed on the market does not comply with the Directives, that manufacturer must—atake immediate corrective measures to ensure that the equipment complies with the Directives;bwithdraw the equipment from the market; orcissue a recall of the equipment.3Where a manufacturer considers that equipment it has placed on the market presents a risk, that manufacturer must immediately inform the TPED competent authority in any relevant member State of the risk, including providing details of any non-compliance with the Directives and any action taken in accordance with paragraph (2).4A manufacturer must record each instance of non-compliance with the Directives and any corrective measure taken and must retain that record for at least 20 years from the date that the non-compliance is discovered.5On receipt of a reasoned request from a TPED competent authority, a manufacturer must—aprovide that authority, in a language that it easily understands, all information and documents necessary to show that the equipment meets the requirements of the Directives; andbcooperate with that authority in any action it takes to eliminate risks posed by that equipment.6This regulation applies to an importer or a distributor as if that person were a manufacturer where the importer or distributor—aplaces equipment on the market under the importer or distributor's own name or trademark; orbmodifies equipment already placed on the market in such a way that compliance with the Directives may be affected.Obligations of Importers19C1An importer must ensure that—athe manufacturer has complied with conformity assessment and drawn up the technical documentation in accordance with the Dangerous Goods Directive;bequipment has been marked in accordance with articles 14 and 15 of the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive;cthe certificate of conformity for the equipment either contains the name and address of the importer or has this information attached to it;dthe conditions in which equipment under the responsibility of the importer is stored and transported do not jeopardise the equipment's compliance with the Dangerous Goods Directive; andethe technical documentation specified in the Dangerous Goods Directive is kept for the period set out in that Directive.2Where an importer knows or has reason to believe that equipment it has placed on the market does not comply with the Directives, that importer must—atake immediate corrective measures to ensure that the equipment complies with the Directives;bwithdraw the equipment from the market; orcissue a recall of the equipment.3Where an importer considers that equipment presents a risk before it has been placed on the market, that importer must inform the manufacturer and the Health and Safety Executive of the risk.4Where an importer considers that equipment it has placed on the market presents a risk, that importer must immediately inform the manufacturer and the TPED competent authority in any relevant member State of the risk, including details of any non-compliance with the Directives and any action taken in accordance with paragraph (2).5An importer must record each instance of non-compliance with the Directives and any corrective measure taken and must retain that record for at least 20 years from the date that the non-compliance is discovered.6On receipt of a reasoned request from a TPED competent authority, an importer must—aprovide that authority, in a language that it easily understands, all information and documents necessary to show that the equipment meets the requirements of the Directives; andcpublish a report.2In carrying out the review the Secretary of State must, so far as is reasonable, have regard to how the Directives are implemented in other member States of the EU.3The report must in particular—aset out the objectives intended to be achieved by these Regulations;bassess the extent to which those objectives are achieved; xmls:
<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1512/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2013/1512" NumberOfProvisions="8" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" xml:lang="en" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Secondary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1512/body/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2013/1512/body" NumberOfProvisions="8"><P1group><Title>Amendments to the Work at Height Regulations 2005</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5" id="regulation-5">
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5/1/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5/1" id="regulation-5-1">
<Pnumber>1</Pnumber>
<P2para><Text>The Work at Height Regulations 2005<FootnoteRef Ref="f00006"/> are amended as follows.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5/2/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5/2" id="regulation-5-2">
<Pnumber>2</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After regulation 8, insert—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="unknown" TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double">
<P1group>
<Title>Dock Operations</Title>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter="">8A</Pnumber>
<P1para><Text Hanging="indented">In relation to work at height where people are engaged in dock operations, every employer shall ensure that Schedule 9 is complied with.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
</P1group>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5/3/made" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/uksi/2013/1512/regulation/5/3" id="regulation-5-3">
<Pnumber>3</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>After Schedule 8, add—</Text>
<BlockAmendment Context="schedule" TargetSubClass="unknown" Format="double" TargetClass="unknown">
<Schedule>
<Number>SCHEDULE<Character Name="NonBreakingSpace"/>9</Number>
<TitleBlock>
<Title>REQUIREMENTS FOR WORK IN DOCKS</Title>
</TitleBlock>
<Reference>Regulation 8A</Reference>
<ScheduleBody>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">1</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In relation to work at height where people are engaged in dock operations, there shall be secure and adequate guardrails at the following places—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>every break, dangerous corner and other dangerous part or edge of a dock, wharf, quay or jetty; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para><Text>every open side of a gangway, footway over a bridge, caisson or dock gate,</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<Text>except in so far as the provision of such guardrails is impracticable because of the nature of the work carried out there and the work is in progress.</Text>
</P1para>
</P1>
<P1>
<Pnumber PuncAfter=".">2</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>In this Schedule—</Text>
<UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“dock gate” means any lock gate or other gate which can close off the entrance to the dock or part of the dock from the sea or other waterway but does not include any gate on land which controls access by vehicles or pedestrians;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“dock operations” means—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the loading or unloading of goods on or from a ship at dock premises;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the embarking or disembarking of passengers on or from a ship at dock premises;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>any activity incidental to the activities in sub-paragraph (a) or (b) which takes place on dock premises, including any of the following—</Text><OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="roman">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the fuelling and provisioning of a ship;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the mooring of a ship;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the storing, sorting, inspecting, checking, weighing or handling of goods;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the movement of goods, passengers or vehicles;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the use of welfare amenities in relation to the activities in sub-paragraph (a), (b) or (c)(i) to (iv);</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>attending dock premises for the purposes of the activities in sub-paragraph (a), (b) or (c)(i) to (v); or the embarking or disembarking on or from a ship of its crew at dock premises,</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
<Text>but does not include—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha" Start="4">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>the loading or unloading of goods or embarking or disembarking of persons on or from a pleasure craft or any activity incidental to those activities; or</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>beach landing operations wholly carried out by serving members of Her Majesty’s Forces or visiting forces within the meaning of the provisions of Part I of the Visiting Forces Act 1952<FootnoteRef Ref="f00007"/> or a combination of both;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“dock premises” means any dock, wharf, quay, jetty or other place at which ships load or unload goods or embark or disembark passengers, together with neighbouring land or water which is used or occupied, or intended to be used or occupied, for those or incidental activities, and any part of a ship when used for those or incidental activities;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“freight container” means a container as defined in regulation 2 of the Freight Containers (Safety Convention) Regulations 1984<FootnoteRef Ref="f00008"/>;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“goods” includes—</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>animals;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>pallets and freight containers;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>waste;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>solid ballast;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>vehicles which are being transported as cargo;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“pleasure craft” means any description of vessel when used solely for sport or recreation, other than for carrying fare paying passengers;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“ship” includes all vessels and hovercraft which operate on water or land and water;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“vehicle” includes all lift trucks, locomotives and rolling-stock, and trailers and semi-trailers and other mechanical plant which moves on wheels, tracks, skids or any combination thereof;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“vessel” means any description of craft used for the transport of goods or passengers or the storage of goods or the accommodation of passengers on water, whether used in navigation or not;</Text>
</Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>“welfare amenities” means–</Text>
<OrderedList Decoration="parens" Type="alpha">
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>sanitary conveniences;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>baths and shower baths;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>washing facilities;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a supply of wholesome drinking water;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>a supply of protective clothing, that is to say, clothing suitable for the protection of the wearer in refrigerated spaces or against dirt from handling dirty goods or against inclement weather;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>accommodation and facilities for changing into clothing worn during working hours and for storing and drying clothing;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>canteens, or accommodation and facilities (including facilities for heating food and boiling water) for workers employed at dock premises to eat meals provided by themselves;</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
<ListItem>
<Para><Text>shelters for use during inclement weather.</Text></Para>
</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
</Para>
</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
</P1para>
</P1>
</ScheduleBody>
</Schedule>
</BlockAmendment>
<AppendText>.</AppendText>
</P2para>
</P2>
</P1para>
</P1></P1group></Body></Secondary></Legislation>
